scope: Theorem 12.2 (Spatial bridge estimates) of the manuscript “Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks” (preprints/Radial-transfer-estimates-and-polygon-length-laws-for-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 02d2e8df0dcf370b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 95. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all h ≥ 1 and every allowed horizontal displacement x, ch−1/4 ≤ Bh ≤ Ch−1/4 , Bh(x) ≤ Ch−5/4 , Bh[diam > Mh] ≤ C(Mh)−1/4 (M ≥ 1). (12.7) Let g : [0, 1] → R be a continuous piecewise linear function with g(0) = 0, and fix ε > 0. The bridge mass restricted to the corridor {(x, y) : 0 ≤ y ≤ h, |x − hg(y/h)| ≤ εh} is at least c(g, ε)h−1/4 for all sufficiently large admissible h. The starting port is fixed and the terminal port is free. For a compact family of such graphs in the uniform topology, the constant and the lower threshold can be chosen uniformly.
